title: Real-time communication: WebSocket, Melody and Centrifugo

videos.script: A page that says a hundred and twelve seats left is true when it loads. On a busy night it is false a few seconds later. {{options}} There are four ways to keep it true: ask again and again, ask and wait, or keep a connection open, one way or both ways. {{news}} The hard part is knowing that something changed. Every sale passes through the database, so the database announces it, with a trigger and LISTEN. {{sse}} Server-sent events need nothing but net/http: one response that never ends. {{ws}} A WebSocket goes both ways, and it has to check which sites may open one. {{libs}} Then Melody, a hub you do not write, and Centrifugo, a server that holds the connections for you. {{scale}} Last, what changes when there is more than one process, and when polling is still the right answer.
